title: What If Mauna Loa's Lava Reached the City of Hilo?

scenes.text: What if Mauna Loa sent lava straight at Hilo? It has come closer than you'd think.
In 1984, a fissure over a mile long opened at 9,350 feet, with lava fountains about 165 feet high.
Lava ran nearly sixteen miles in four days, roughly four miles every single day.
By then it was about four miles from Hilo, and the flow slowed as the supply faded.
In 1881, a flow stopped just 1.1 miles from Hilo's bayfront. In 2022, one stalled 1.7 miles from a highway.
Mauna Loa has erupted 33 times since 1843. So far, the lava has always stopped short.

description:
What if Mauna Loa's lava reached Hilo?
In 1984 it ran nearly sixteen miles in four days and stopped about four miles short.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Would you live near an active volcano? Drop your own 'what if' too.
